title: Orchard and Atlas
premise: In 1847, in a fog-bound port city where cartography is a licensed monopoly, Beatrix Fairweather completes the atlas his late master died drafting, only to find a sealed letter hidden in the plate proofs: proof that the merchant family bankrolling the atlas engineered a famine-relief scheme that diverted grain and let thousands die. When the family's heirs move to buy the atlas outright and burn its marginalia, Beatrix—along with a disgraced printer, a widowed customs clerk, and his master's estranged daughter—must smuggle the evidence into print before the victors' historians seal the record. The atlas is published in a small, dangerous run, the family's name enters the record at terrible cost, and Beatrix learns that history happens to everyone; the only choice is whether you write it or are written.
about_author: Paloma Almeida is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suppressed municipal records in coastal trading cities. Orchard and Atlas is her second novel, following a well-received debut about lighthouse keepers and debt.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Paper
chapters.summary: Beatrix Fairweather, POV. Finishing his dead master's atlas in a cold workshop, Beatrix inks the final coastline and reflects that maps record places, never people. Emotional beat: quiet grief and the comfort of anonymity.

chapters.title: A Letter Under Seal
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. While checking plate proofs, he finds a sealed letter sewn into the atlas's binding, written in his master's dying hand and naming the Voss family in a grain-diversion plot. Emotional beat: dread cracking open a safe life.

chapters.title: The Voss Offer
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. The Voss heirs arrive with a generous offer to buy the atlas outright, plates and marginalia included. Beatrix refuses before he understands why. Emotional beat: first taste of power pressing on him.

chapters.title: The Printer Who Lost Everything
chapters.summary: Odile Ferrant, POV. A disgraced printer whose press was seized for sedition reads the letter and recognizes the famine year that killed her brother. Emotional beat: rage finding a purpose.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. He deciphers his master's map annotations—coordinates of warehouses, grain tonnages disguised as survey notes. The atlas itself is the evidence. Emotional beat: awe at the master's hidden courage.

chapters.title: The Customs Clerk's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tobias Renner, POV. A widowed customs clerk confirms the letter's numbers against seized manifests, risking his pension. Emotional beat: a cautious man choosing to be counted.

chapters.title: The Master's Daughter
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. He tracks down Elin Marchetti, the master's estranged daughter, who resents the atlas that consumed her father. Emotional beat: bitterness meeting a shared inheritance.

chapters.title: A Fire in the Archive
chapters.summary: Tobias, POV. The municipal archive burns, destroying corroborating manifests; Tobias saves one box and is now a marked man. Emotional beat: fear hardening into defiance.

chapters.title: What the Victorians Will Write
chapters.summary: Elin, POV. Elin attends a Voss banquet and hears the official famine narrative being polished for the histories. Emotional beat: nausea at history being authored in advance.

chapters.title: The Price of Staying Invisible
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. The Vosses escalate: threats to his guild license, then to his person. He realizes invisibility was always a luxury others paid for. Emotional beat: loss of innocence.

chapters.title: Orchard Road
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. The fugitives regroup at a derelict orchard farmhouse Odile's brother once owned; the found family takes shape around a kitchen table and a hidden press. Emotional beat: fragile belonging.

chapters.title: Setting the Type
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. They begin setting the exposé by hand, page by page, while Beatrix drafts a map of the diversion routes as its centerpiece. Emotional beat: purpose forged in secret.

chapters.title: The Informant
chapters.summary: Tobias, POV. A trusted colleague betrays their location to the Voss agent, Mr. Quill. Tobias must choose between warning the others and protecting his daughter. Emotional beat: loyalty under the knife.

chapters.title: Quill's Visit
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Quill offers Beatrix absolution, money, and his master's reputation restored—if he surrenders the letter. Beatrix sees the corruption's human face. Emotional beat: temptation resisted at cost.

chapters.title: The Raid on the Orchard
chapters.summary: Elin, POV. Soldiers raze the farmhouse; the press is smashed, Tobias is arrested, and the nearly finished edition burns. Elin saves the type cases. Emotional beat: grief and fury entwined.

chapters.title: What Cannot Be Printed
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. With the press gone, Elin proposes the unthinkable: publish the truth as the atlas itself, plates and all, through the guild's own licensing channel. Emotional beat: desperate ingenuity.

chapters.title: The Guild Vote
chapters.summary: Tobias, freed on a technicality, POV. The found family petitions the cartographers' guild to license the atlas as drawn, marginalia included; the vote is bought, then overturned by one defector. Emotional beat: solidarity arriving from unexpected quarters.

chapters.title: Running the Plates
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. A night-long dash through the port to move plates to a sympathetic naval print shop, pursued by Quill's men. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Atlas Goes to Press
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. The atlas prints at dawn with the evidence in plain sight; Quill arrives too late, and Beatrix signs the colophon with his own name for the first time. Emotional beat: claiming authorship of history.

chapters.title: The Reckoning
chapters.summary: Elin, POV. The atlas spreads through the city; the Voss heirs face inquiry, and Quill, cut loose, trades testimony for leniency. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfect but real.

chapters.title: What It Cost
chapters.summary: Tobias, POV. The survivors bury the master beside the orchard, and Tobias reckons with the daughter who nearly lost him. Emotional beat: mourning the price paid for the record.

chapters.title: A Map With Names
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Years later, Beatrix teaches apprentices and adds a final plate to a new edition: not coastlines, but names—the dead of the famine year. Emotional beat: peace, and the end of invisibility.
